card.name: Inside the word metastatic in cancer indications
card.fires_on: The ending "atic" of "metastatic" in cancer indication lines, usually after "unresectable", "locally advanced" or "MSI-H" and before a tumor type such as TNBC, colorectal cancer or NSCLC. Also fires on the space after "every" in dosing-schedule lines.

modes.label: metastatic ending
modes.description: The final piece of "metastatic" in a cancer indication before a tumor name.
modes.example: unresectable locally advanced or metast<<atic>> TNBC 200 mg every

modes.label: space after every
modes.description: The space after "every" in an oncology dosing schedule, before the number of weeks.
modes.example: recurrent locally advanced MCC 500 mg every<< >>4 weeks Until disease progression

card.plain: It marks the word metastatic when it is spelled out in a cancer-treatment indication.
